title: Sunmere Online – a free fantasy MMORPG I built with AI agents (browser, PC and Android)
author: Realistic_Warthog_85
selftext:
Sunmere Online is a small fantasy MMORPG you can play for free in your browser, on Windows or on Android: https://dhrubo95zd.itch.io/sunmere-online

There are seven classes, a main story, dungeons, raids and houses you can walk into, all set in a world of steam-powered machines instead of monsters. The part I'm proudest of is the combat. Instead of a bar full of 20 skills, each class has seven, and using two of them back to back fuses them into a new move. For example, the Knight's rising slash into his overhead strike becomes a leap into the air and a slam back down. There's also a Path of Exile style skill web that changes how your skills work, and bosses stagger after their big attacks, which is the moment to hit them with your best combo. The world is online 24/7, and there are helper bots around (always marked as bots) so it never feels completely empty.

I can't code, so the whole thing was made by working with AI. I used Claude Code for all of the programming. I'd explain what I wanted in plain words, it would write a plan, and then build it step by step. For the bigger jobs, like reworking all seven classes, it ran several agents side by side, one per class, which felt more like managing a small team than coding. What helped most was getting it to test its own work: it runs the game in a hidden window, takes screenshots, records every combo frame by frame, and has bots play through every quest and fight every boss. That caught things I'd never have noticed, like one class doing almost double the damage of the others.

The skill icons and portraits are painted with Codex. That was the hardest part, because my game has strict art rules (no faces, no animals, no stars or crosses) and the image models break them constantly, so every picture gets checked closely and plenty got redone. I also tried AI image-to-3D for one character, but it looked out of place next to everything else, so it was replaced with a normal rigged model and free animations.

Even the server was an AI job. It started on my own PC, then a free Google server that was far too slow, and now it runs on a free Oracle server after the AI reworked it so enemies far away from players go to sleep, which made it light enough to stay up all the time.

The biggest thing I learned is that AI is fast but sometimes confidently wrong, so making it check and measure its own work mattered far more than clever prompts.

It's still early and rough in places, so any feedback is very welcome, especially on what feels clunky.
